title: The kingfisher that redesigned a bullet train

scenes.headline: This bird redesigned a bullet train.
Its beak enters water with barely a splash.
scenes.body: The beak widens smoothly from tip to head, so it parts the water instead of slapping it.

scenes.headline: Japan's 500 Series trains had a problem: tunnel booms.
scenes.body: At speed they pushed a pressure wave ahead and burst out of tunnels with a bang.

scenes.label: less electricity after the kingfisher-shaped nose
scenes.body: Quieter in tunnels, and about 10% faster than the train before it.

caption:
A kingfisher's beak fixed the bullet train's tunnel boom.

The redesigned 500 Series nose is about 15 m long and almost round in cross-section, copying the way the beak widens gradually from its tip.

Source: AskNature / Biomimicry Institute (Eiji Nakatsu, JR West). Footage: common kingfisher. Photos/video: Wikimedia Commons (credits on screen).
notes: A fact with a twist ending (bird to train) and a hard number payoff; all footage is the common kingfisher that inspired the design.
